title: Working with Git knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Working with Git”?
options: Running Git commands from Bash scripts
questions.answer_key: Running Git commands from Bash scripts
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Running Git commands from Bash scripts” under lesson 153, “Working with Git”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Working with Git”?
options: Check external command versions, validate input, set timeouts, and handle failures explicitly.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
questions.answer_key: Check external command versions, validate input, set timeouts, and handle failures explicitly.
questions.explanation: Check external command versions, validate input, set timeouts, and handle failures explicitly. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Working with Git”?
options: Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
